verdict.rationale: Temporal's own Worker Versioning feature lets each Workflow type declare a Versioning Behavior of Pinned or Auto-Upgrade, built on Worker Deployments and Worker Deployment Versions. Pinned is the mechanism for letting in-flight runs finish on the version they started with while new code is deployed. A community user confirms that determinism is the core constraint this feature addresses. missing for 10: an explicit documented statement that Pinned executions stay on their starting version through completion, rollout/ramp and patching details, and independent hands-on corroboration of safe deploys without non-determinism errors.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I deploy new workflow code while in-flight runs finish on the version they started with — versioning without breaking determinism

citations.quote: You can declare each Workflow type to have a Versioning Behavior, either Pinned or Auto-Upgrade, in your Workflow config
Worker Deployments ... Worker Deployment Versions ... Versioning Behaviors
What it requires in exchange is full determinism.
